propositions: Full-suite scheduler load causes intermittent false-positive stall classification of dribbling git-fetch transfers that pass in isolation.
Shared 2-second stall-detection window applied to both zero-byte stall controls and above-floor negative controls creates scheduler-sensitive race conditions.
Cumulative bytes-owed catch-up calculation fixes repeated wake-up delays but cannot recover after libcurl has already aborted during a single uninterrupted scheduling gap.
Test pacing helper sends rate//10 bytes per 0.1-second wake-up, so delayed wake-ups reduce actual throughput below the promised rate and can trigger false low-speed aborts.

Production 10-second window must remain unchanged; test remediation requires separating fast zero-byte stall detection from one production-window dribble integration test with deterministic pacing coverage.
